{{short description|Chinese physicist}}
'''Laura Na Liu''' (born 1979) is a Chinese physicist focused on researching [[Nanophotonics|nano-optics]] of three-dimensional meta materials as it applies to [[biology]] and [[chemistry]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2019/the_optical_society_names_laura_na_liu_the_2019_ad/|title=The Optical Society Names Laura Na Liu the 2019 Adolph Lomb Medal Winner|last=|first=|date=|website=The Optical Society|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/inhalt.uni-stuttgart-reifung-im-reinraum.04ac2aff-e092-4fb1-9748-e8f00df9d470.html|title=Maturation in the Clean Room|last=Schafer|first=Martin|date=March 23, 2010|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=February 9, 2020}}</ref> After receiving her undergraduate and master's degree in [[China]], she has had many global opportunities for education and research including [[Germany]] and the [[United States of America]].<ref name=":0" /> Today, she is a professor at [[University of Stuttgart]] in Germany.<ref name=":0" /> She has received several awards for her contributions in the field of optics.

== Biography ==
Liu has completed her higher education all over the world. As a young woman, Liu completed her studies in [[Beijing]] and [[Hong Kong]] before she moved to Germany and earned a doctorate degree in physics at [[University of Stuttgart]] in 2009.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> In order to succeed, she had to overcome the culture shock between the two countries' lifestyles.<ref name=":1" /> A year later she became a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of California]], Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Hui |last2=Yu |first2=Cun |date=2024-01-23 |title=Light People: Professor Laura Na Liu |journal=Light: Science & Applications |language=en |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=26 |doi=10.1038/s41377-023-01356-3  |doi-access=free|pmid=38263272 |issn=2047-7538|pmc=10805779 |bibcode=2024LSA....13...26W }}</ref> In 2011, she transitioned again to [[Rice University]] to be a Texas Instrument Visiting professor. The following year, Liu joined the [[Max-Planck Institute]] for Intelligent Systems and led the "Small Nanoplasmonics" research group.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://is.mpg.de/news/laura-na-liu-receives-2018-kavli-foundation-early-career-award|title=Laura Na Liu receives 2018 Kavli Foundation Early Career Award|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> Since 2015, Liu moved back to Germany and is a professor at [[University of Stuttgart]]. Liu has also been married since receiving her degrees in China.<ref name=":1" />

== Scientific contributions ==
Only being a PhD candidate before 2009, she published 11 papers before receiving her degree.<ref name=":1" />

Through Liu's research efforts, she has become a leading scientist in optics as it pertains to [[DNA]] and [[catalytic chemistry]]. Much of the research she conducts is on the [[Nanometre|nano]] (less than 3&nbsp;nm) level.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Na|last2=Tang|first2=Ming L.|last3=Hentschel|first3=Mario|last4=Giessen|first4=Harald|last5=Alivisatos|first5=A. Paul|date=2011|title=Nanoantenna-enhanced gas sensing in a single tailored nanofocus|journal=CLEO:2011 - Laser Applications to Photonic Applications|volume=10|issue=8|pages=631–6|location=Washington, D.C.|publisher=OSA|doi=10.1364/cleo_at.2011.pdpc11|pmid=21572410|isbn=978-1-55752-910-7}}</ref> Liu designs and studies 3D meta-materials which are classified as smaller than visible light's wavelength.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Na|last2=Guo|first2=Hongcang|last3=Fu|first3=Liwei|last4=Kaiser|first4=Stefan|last5=Schweizer|first5=Heinz|last6=Giessen|first6=Harald|date=2007-12-02|title=Three-dimensional photonic metamaterials at optical frequencies|journal=Nature Materials|volume=7|issue=1|pages=31–37|doi=10.1038/nmat2072|pmid=18059275|s2cid=42254771|issn=1476-1122}}</ref>  These can play an important role to understand small scale biological structures and even metal interactions. In addition, she was involved in designing an absorber device for [[Image sensor|optical sensing]], even through metal interference.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Na|last2=Mesch|first2=Martin|last3=Weiss|first3=Thomas|last4=Hentschel|first4=Mario|last5=Giessen|first5=Harald|date=2010-07-14|title=Infrared Perfect Absorber and Its Application As Plasmonic Sensor|journal=Nano Letters|volume=10|issue=7|pages=2342–2348|doi=10.1021/nl9041033|pmid=20560590|bibcode=2010NanoL..10.2342L |issn=1530-6984}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Liu has been a prolific publisher since 2008. A few of her most cited articles {{as of|2020|lc=y}} tracked by [[Web of Science]] are:<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/2552942/na-liu/metrics/|title=Web of Science Researcher ID|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

* Liu, N., Mesch, M., Weiss, T., Hentschel, M., & Giessen, H. (2010). [[doi:10.1021/NL9041033|"Infrared Perfect Absorber and Its Application as Plasmonic Sensor"]] ''Nano Letters'', ''10''(7), 2342–2348. [[doi:10.1021/NL9041033|doi.10.1021/NL9041033]]
*Liu, N., Langguth, L., Weiss, T., Kästel, J., Fleischhauer, M., Pfau, T., & Giessen, H. (2009). [[doi:10.1021/NL9041033|"Plasmonic analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency at the Drude damping limit"]]  ''Nature Materials'', ''8''(9), 758–762.[[doi:10.1021/NL9041033|doi.org/10.1021/NL9041033]]
*Liu, N., Mesch, M., Weiss, T., Hentschel, M., Giessen, H. (2010) [[doi:10.1021/NL902621D|"Planar Metamaterial Analogue of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency for Plasmonic Sensing"]]  ''Nano Letters,'' 10(4),1103-1107 [[doi:10.1021/NL902621D|doi.10.1021/NL902621D]]
* Liu, N., Tan, M., Hentshcel, M., Giessen, H., Alivisatos, A. (2011) [[doi:10.1038/NMAT3029|"Nanoantenna-enhanced gas sensing in a single tailored nanofocus"]] ''Nature Materials'' 10, 631–636 [[doi:10.1038/NMAT3029|doi. 10.1038/NMAT3029]]
*Liu, N., Guo, H., Fu, L., Kaiser, S., Schweizer, H., Giessen, H. (2008) [[doi:10.1038/NMAT2072|"Three-dimensional photonic metamaterials at optical frequencies"]]  ''Nature Materials,'' 7, 31-37  [[doi:10.1038/NMAT2072|doi 10.1038/NMAT2072]]

== Awards ==
By incorporating chemistry and biology into nano-photonics, Liu has advanced the multidisciplinary collaboration and research within this field.<ref name=":0" /> She has gained much recognition for her hard work within the field at such a young age. Over the years, Liu has received many awards including:

*2023 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] "for seminal contributions to the development of three-dimensional optical metamaterials and leadership in paving the new research field of DNA-based 3D dynamic nanophotonics"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2023|title=2023 Fellows|work=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2023-10-19}}</ref>
*2020 Fellow of Optica<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Optical Society Announces 2020 Fellows Class {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2019/the_optical_society_announces_2020_fellows_class/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>{{Non-primary source needed|date=January 2025}}
* 2019: [[Adolph Lomb Medal]] (awards a young scientist or engineer who has greatly advanced the field of optics by The Optical Society)<ref name=":0" />
*2019: Nano Letters Young Investigator Lectureship Award (awards large contribution in the field of [[nano-science and technology]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://axial.acs.org/2019/04/30/2019-nano-letters-young-investigator-lectureship-award/|title=Professor Laura Na Liu Wins 2019 Nano Letters Young Investigator Lectureship Award|last=Marcus|first=Anderson|date=30 April 2019|website=ACS Publications|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> 
*2018 & 2019: Highly Cited Researcher by the [[Web of Science]]<ref name=":3" />
*2018: Kavli Foundation Early Career Lectureship in Materials Science (awards young researchers who show great potential for leadership within their career and advances the field greatly by the [[Materials Research Society]]; winners are also given a monetary prize and the ability to present their research at the award ceremony)<ref name=":2" />
*2018: Rudolf-Kaiser Prize<ref name=":0" /> 
*2016: [[IUPAP Young Scientist Prize]] in Optics (awards 8 years of excellent research after completion of Ph.D; winners are also given a monetary prize, medal and ability to present their research at the award conference)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iupap.org/young-scientist-prize/|title=The Young Scientist Prize|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> 
*2015: Light 2015 Young Women in Photonics Award (given by the [[European Optical Society]])<ref name=":2" /> 
*2014: [[Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Preis|Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Award]] (awards young researchers within the country who have had quick career advancements by the [[German Research Foundation]] and are highly encouraged to continue their hard work; winners are given a monetary prize)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.is.mpg.de/news/laura-na-liu-awarded-with-heinz-maier-leibnitz-prize|title=Laura Na Liu awarded with Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Prize|last=|first=|date=|website=Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems|archive-url=|archive-date=}}</ref> 
* 2014: European Research Council Starting Grant<ref name=":2" />
* 2013: Elisabeth Schiemann-Kolleg of the Max Planck Society Fellowship<ref name=":2" />
* 2010: [[Hertha Sponer Prize]] of the [[German Research Foundation]]
